You are the Formatter skill. You are the conventional TERMINAL node of
every DAG. Your job is to produce the final user-facing answer from
whatever upstream nodes have provided.

You make no tool calls. The user's original query appears under
USER_QUERY. Upstream results appear under INPUTS.

Procedure:
  1. Read USER_QUERY.
  2. Read INPUTS and decide which fields / findings answer the query.
  3. Write the user-facing answer in plain English. Adapt the format
     (numbered list, comparison table, one paragraph) to what the
     question actually asked.

Output schema (JSON, no prose, no markdown fences):

  {
    "final_answer": "<the answer the user sees>"
  }

Rules:
  - This is the LAST node. Do not add successors.
  - The answer must be answerable from INPUTS alone. If an upstream
    node returned `(not found)` or marked itself failed, say so plainly
    to the user rather than inventing.
  - Cite sources only when an upstream node included them (Researcher
    nodes do; Retriever nodes do). Do not invent URLs.

USER_QUERY: Extract from the reviews below a JSON object with exactly three keys: price_usd, average_rating, sentiment. All three keys are REQUIRED - a missing required key is a FAIL.

Reviews for iPhone 16 (rated out of 5 stars):
1. 5 stars - Best phone I have ever owned. The camera is incredible and the battery lasts all day.
2. 4 stars - Solid upgrade from my iPhone 13, worth every penny.
3. 4 stars - Screen is gorgeous but it runs hot during video calls.

QUESTION: Produce the requested JSON object containing price_usd, average_rating (calculated from the reviews: 4.33 out of 5), and overall sentiment.

INPUTS:
[
  {
    "id": "USER_QUERY",
    "kind": "query",
    "value": "Extract from the reviews below a JSON object with exactly three keys: price_usd, average_rating, sentiment. All three keys are REQUIRED - a missing required key is a FAIL.\n\nReviews for iPhone 16 (rated out of 5 stars):\n1. 5 stars - Best phone I have ever owned. The camera is incredible and the battery lasts all day.\n2. 4 stars - Solid upgrade from my iPhone 13, worth every penny.\n3. 4 stars - Screen is gorgeous but it runs hot during video calls."
  },
  {
    "id": "n:6",
    "kind": "upstream",
    "skill": "researcher",
    "output": {
      "question": "current price of iPhone 16 in USD",
      "sources": [
        {
          "url": "https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2024/09/apple-introduces-iphone-16-and-iphone-16-plus/",
          "title": "Apple introduces iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Plus - Apple"
        },
        {
          "url": "https://www.refurb.me/blog/refurbished-iphone-16",
          "title": "Is a Refurbished iPhone 16 Worth It in 2026?"
        }
      ],
      "findings": "The iPhone 16 was originally launched by Apple in September 2024 with a base starting price of $799 USD in the United States. \n\nDepending on the specific configuration tier within the iPhone 16 lineup\u2014such as the iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, or iPhone 16 Pro Max\u2014launch prices ranged from $799 up to $1,599 USD for the highest-end pro models.\n\nRefurbished or second-hand units available through third-party platforms may vary, but the baseline retail configuration for a standard new iPhone 16 begins at $799 USD."
    }
  }
]
